q: AI coding agents spend a substantial fraction of their tool calls on undirected codebase exploration.
r: Include: controlled experiment on architecture-descriptor context files (S-expression, JSON, YAML, Markdown) given to coding agents, group (b).

r: EC6: group (c) evaluation built on SWE-bench Verified issue repair, always excluded even with a method contribution.

q: Current practice tends toward what we call Monolithic Context Injection
r: Include: skill-based modular context for coding agents with a controlled CMS case study measuring tokens and quality, group (b).
EC6: single-shot evaluation of code representation on SWE-bench Verified issue resolution, issue repair, always excluded.

q: AI coding agents increasingly rely on skills: structured context bundles, typically a SKILL.md file with a YAML header and Markdown body
r: Include: empirical study of agent skills (SKILL.md context files) for coding agents and how they are adapted and maintained, group (b).

q: an application augmentation layer for AI coding agents.
r: Include: Plugin-Agent-Skill hierarchy encoding conventions and a six-phase workflow for coding agents; weak evidence but context mechanisms, group (b).

q: We establish a paired without-skill/with-skill intervention protocol to measure how access to structured Alipay payment guidance changes adherence to product-specific APIs
r: Include: besides a single-domain benchmark it evaluates a skill (context mechanism) for coding agents in paired conditions, group (b).

q: Claude Code is a command-line coding agent: a user converses with a model that can read and edit files, run commands, and iterate toward a goal, all within a single session.
sec: 2.1 Claude Code, subagents, and agent teams
r: Include: file-based persistent state, roles, hooks and skills for Claude Code teams (memory and instruction files), group (b); no evaluation but not an EC3 type.

q: Experimental results showed limited benefits from developer-specific personalization
r: Include: evaluates personalized and generic skills for coding agents with replay experiments, group (b).
